From B2 First, practice paper 1, reading part 5

Starting from scratch at forty

For most of my adult life, I told people that I wasn't musical. It was something I had decided at the age of nine, when my piano teacher sighed loudly every time I played a wrong note, and I had never had any reason to question it.

Why had the writer always believed that she was not musical?

  1. Her daughter was a much better musician than she was.
  2. A teacher's reaction to her mistakes had convinced her as a child.
  3. She had tried several instruments without success.
  4. Her friends had told her that she could not sing.

Every word in a paper can be tapped for its meaning and forms while you practise.

The exams

Which exams the papers cover

There are two practice papers for each of seven exams: four Cambridge English Qualifications from Cambridge University Press & Assessment, the two versions of IELTS, run by the British Council, IDP and Cambridge, and the TOEFL iBT from ETS.

Results

How the exams report results

None of these exams gives a single mark out of 100, and each reports its result differently.

  • Cambridge: each paper gets a score on the Cambridge English Scale, and the overall score is their average, with no minimum for a single paper. The lowest overall score that passes is 140 for B1 Preliminary, 160 for B2 First, 180 for C1 Advanced and 200 for C2 Proficiency.
  • IELTS: each test gets a band from 0 to 9, in whole or half bands, and the overall band is their mean, rounded to the nearest half band. There is no pass or fail: each university, employer or authority sets the band it requires.
  • TOEFL iBT: each section is scored from 1 to 6, and the overall score is their average, rounded to the nearest half band. For two years after January 2026 the report also gives a comparable score on the older 0–120 scale. There is no pass mark: each university or programme sets the score it requires.
  • Glossa's papers show the share of points in each section. They do not turn it into a Cambridge English Scale score, an IELTS band or a TOEFL score.

Papers to practise on, and a course to learn from

Honest limits

How the practice papers differ from the real exams

  • No score, band or grade is given. A paper shows the share of points per section and cannot tell you which Cambridge grade, IELTS band or TOEFL score you would get.
  • Reading and listening are shorter than in the real exams, usually about half the questions with the time cut to match. Writing is full length.
  • There is no speaking test, except Listen and Repeat in the TOEFL papers. Glossa cannot yet assess free speech the way examiners do.
  • Recordings can be replayed, and each is read by one voice with the speakers' names. Play each one as often as the real exam does: twice for Cambridge, once for IELTS and TOEFL.
  • Some marking is simpler. Every question is worth one point, while some Cambridge parts give two marks. In IELTS writing the two tasks count the same in Glossa, while in the real test Task 2 counts twice as much.
  • The TOEFL papers are not adaptive: everyone gets the same tasks.
  • The papers use American spelling. Cambridge and IELTS accept it when it is used consistently.
  • Words can be tapped for their meaning while you practise; the real exams allow no dictionary.

Questions

Common questions

Is Glossa connected with Cambridge, IELTS or ETS?
No. Glossa is not connected with Cambridge University Press & Assessment, the British Council, IDP or ETS. The papers follow their published test descriptions, with original content.
Which exam should I take?
Whoever asks you for a certificate decides which exams and scores they accept, so check with them first. IELTS Academic is for university study and professional registration, IELTS General Training for work, training and migration, and the TOEFL iBT is asked for by universities in the United States and many other countries. Cambridge exams certify one level each, from B1 to C2.
I need IELTS for a visa or residence permit. Does this help?
The papers practise the IELTS task formats, but they do not predict a band. The immigration authority of the country decides which tests and bands it accepts and sets the other conditions, so check its requirements before you book.
What is free?
The whole English course from A1 to C1, the grammar reference, word practice, the traps and the placement test are free, with 5 Ask AI questions a day. The exam papers, conversations, stories, specializations and the other extras are part of Premium.
Can I study with explanations in my own language?
Yes. The same course, with the same exam papers, is available with explanations in Russian, Ukrainian, Finnish, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian and French, with translation exercises both ways.
